title: Soft C (/s/) and Soft G (/dʒ/) Expanded
objectives: Predict soft C /s/ and soft G /dʒ/ before E, I, Y
Recognize Germanic hard G exceptions (get, give, girl)
Master C and G decoding in multi-syllable words

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Present the pronunciation/reading rule for: Soft C (/s/) and Soft G (/dʒ/) Expanded. Use the 14 Gabarit fields to clarify rule, system, logic, and exceptions.

teacherNotes.title: Anticipated Problems & Solutions (CELTA Standard)
teacherNotes.content:
⚠️ Problem: Learner applies soft G rule to 'give' and says /dʒɪv/.
💡 Solution: Memorize 'The 4 Gs': Get, Give, Girl, Gift = Hard /g/!

elements.content: Gabarit 14 Champs: Soft C (/s/) and Soft G (/dʒ/) Expanded
1. Definition: C and G change from hard sounds (/k/, /g/) to soft sounds (/s/, /dʒ/) depending on the following vowel.
2. Rule: Before E, I, Y = Soft C (/s/ city, face) and Soft G (/dʒ/ gem, giant). Before A, O, U = Hard C (/k/ cat) and Hard G (/g/ go).
3. Why? Latin/Romance palatalization altered C and G before front vowels E, I, Y.
4. How to recognize? Check the letter immediately following C or G.
5. Common examples: city, face, cycle, gem, giant, gym vs cat, coat, cup, go, got, gum
6. Counter-examples: Germanic root words with hard G before E/I: get, give, girl, gift, begin, finger.
7. Exceptions: get /ɡɛt/, give /ɡɪv/, girl /ɡɜːrl/, gift /ɡɪft/ (Germanic hard G exceptions).
8. Common mistakes: Pronouncing 'city' with /k/ or 'get' with /dʒ/.
9. Mnemonic / Hint: C and G soft before E, I, Y! Soft C is 100% reliable; Soft G has Germanic hard exceptions!
10. Key vocabulary: soft C, soft G, hard C, hard G, palatalization, Germanic exceptions
11. Frequency: ★★★★★ (Essential)
12. CEFR Level: 🟡 A2
13. Associated Visual: 🍦 Soft ice cream cone for E, I, Y vs Hard rock for A, O, U.
14. Key Takeaway: C/G + E, I, Y = Soft! Remember exceptions: get, give, girl!

teacherNotes.title: Teacher CCQ Script
teacherNotes.content: Ask these concept checking questions to verify rule understanding without translation:

elements.content: Rule Understanding Check (CCQ):
CCQ 1: What sound does C make before E, I, Y? (/s/ soft sound)
CCQ 2: Is 'city' pronounced with /k/ or /s/? (/s/ soft C)
CCQ 3: Why do 'get' and 'girl' have a hard /g/ sound before E and I? (They are Germanic exceptions)

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Auditory discrimination, minimal pairs, and guided oral drill repetition.

elements.content: Identify whether C or G is HARD or SOFT:
🎯 Item: city ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: Soft C (/s/)
🎯 Item: gem ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: Soft G (/dʒ/)
🎯 Item: girl ➔ Answer / Pronunciation: Hard G exception (/g/)
